An empty document has no records at all. Fields are never trimmed, and an empty field is preserved wherever it appears, including at the start or end of a record.

A field is quoted only when the quote character is its very first character: there, the field runs to the matching closing quote, a doubled quote character stands for one literal quote, and delimiters and line terminators inside the quotes are data rather than separators. A quote character anywhere else in a field is ordinary text. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. goal.objective:
`src/csv.js` must export `parse`, `stringify`, `escapeField` and the error class `CsvError`. `parse(text, options)` returns an array of records, each an array of field strings. A leading U+FEFF byte-order mark is dropped; anywhere else U+FEFF is ordinary data. Records are terminated by CRLF, LF or a lone CR, and a single terminator at the very end of the document closes the last record without starting an empty one, so `"a\n"` and `"a"` both read as one record while `"a\n\n"` reads as two and `"\n"` reads as one record holding one empty field. An empty document has no records at all. Fields are never trimmed, and an empty field is preserved wherever it appears, including at the start or end of a record.

A field is quoted only when the quote character is its very first character: there, the field runs to the matching closing quote, a doubled quote character stands for one literal quote, and delimiters and line terminators inside the quotes are data rather than separators. A quote character anywhere else in a field is ordinary text. After a closing quote only a delimiter, a line terminator or the end of the document may follow. `options.delimiter` (default `,`) and `options.quote` (default `"`) each take one UTF-16 code unit; they must differ from each other and neither may be a line terminator. `options.strictWidth` makes every record after the first have to match the first record's field count; without it ragged records are returned as they are.

Every failure throws `CsvError`. Positional failures carry a 1-based `line` and, where a single character is at fault, a 1-based `column` counted in UTF-16 code units from the start of that line: `unterminated quoted field` points at the opening quote, and `unexpected character after closing quote: b` points at the offending character, both accounting for line breaks that occurred inside a quoted field. `expected 2 fields, got 1` carries the line the offending record starts on. Bad arguments throw without a position: `input must be a string`, `delimiter must be a single character`, `quote must be a single character`, `delimiter and quote must differ`, `delimiter and quote must not be line terminators`.

`escapeField(value, options)` returns the text for one field. A string is used as it is; `null` and `undefined` become the empty field; booleans and finite numbers are converted with `String`; anything else throws (`unsupported field value: NaN` for non-finite numbers, `unsupported field type: object` otherwise). The field is quoted, doubling every embedded quote character, when it contains the delimiter, the quote character, CR, LF or U+FEFF, or when `options.alwaysQuote` is set. `stringify(rows, options)` writes each record's escaped fields joined by the delimiter and followed by `options.newline` (default CRLF, and it must be CRLF, LF or CR), including after the last record, and prepends the byte-order mark when `options.bom` is set. `stringify` throws `CsvError` for input that is not an array (`rows must be an array`), a record that is not an array (`record 1 is not an array`) and a record with no fields (`record 0 has no fields`). Reading a document this module wrote, with the same options, must return exactly the records it was given. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
